To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the problem of ensuring the consistency of service composition can be reduced to the problem of ensuring consistency of service orchestration; (2) the latter problem can be solved by checking the consistency of the orchestration of the service against its interface; and (3) the consistency of the interface can be checked by verifying a set of properties that can be derived from the interface specification.
we have developed a formal framework for the specification of service-oriented applications that is based on a formal algebra for service-oriented systems.
we have developed a novel component algebra that allows us to model and reason about the consistency of the composition of service orchestrations and interfaces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a formal foundation and associated techniques for service composition and service binding.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed a formal model of service composition, and a set of techniques that allow for the consistency and correctness of service composition to be checked at design-time, and thus, for the run-time binding of services to be supported in a safe manner.
our approach provides a novel and promising framework for ensuring the consistency of service binding in service-oriented computing.
we have developed techniques for the verification of consistency of composition in the presence of dynamic service binding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a formal model for the composition of services that is based on the notion of asynchronous relational nets, we have developed a framework to check the consistency of service compositions, and we have developed a tool to support the consistency checking of service composition.
we have proposed a novel algebraic approach for service-oriented computing that allows the composition of services to be guaranteed at run time.

we propose a component algebra for the design of applications in a service-oriented computing environment, where service orchestrations are modelled as relational nets and service interfaces as relational types.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by combining the use of a component algebra with the use of logical interfaces, we can provide an approach to service composition that is both flexible and predictable, i.e., it is flexible because it allows the service binding process to be driven by the application, while at the same time being predictable because it allows the consistency of composition, and thus the correctness of the application, to be ensured.
the consistency of composition can be ensured by means of a static analysis that exploits the structure and the semantics of the component models.
the consistency of service binding is not only a matter of matching functional properties but requires also the checking of properties of service orchestrators.
